## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage

## Goal

**User story:** As a player, I want each kill to hand out fewer power-ups as the campaign progresses, so the upgrades I have earned stay meaningful.

Implements "Desired change" step 3 and the parent AC "Power-up supply per enemy falls with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

- Replace the flat `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE` comparison in `PlayScene._maybeDropPowerUp` with the level-resolved `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)`.
- Scale the small-asteroid Extra Life roll by the same ratio (`extraLifeDropChance(level, rules)` where the level is resolved).
- Resolve the level from the live campaign (`WaveManager.currentLevel()?.level`), falling back to level 1 when unknown.
- Keep `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE` exported and documented as the level-1 base value so existing importers keep their meaning.
- Document the per-level source in code comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every kill-time drop roll in `PlayScene` uses the per-level chance; level 1 behaviour is exactly unchanged and level 10 is at most 30 % of the level-1 rate.
- The Extra Life roll scales proportionally with the same ratio.
- Drop types/weights, the mineral kill-drop rule and timed weapon/power-up effects are unchanged.
- The test-first item's tests pass and the existing `PlayScene` tests pass.
- No hard-coded per-level numbers in the scene — all values come from the shared module/rules.

- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **Power-up supply per enemy falls with level** — Every kill-time drop roll in `PlayScene` uses the per-level chance, so the L10 per-kill drop chance is **≤ 30 % of the L1 chance**; the Extra Life roll scales proportionally. Drop types/weights and the timed weapon/power-up effects are unchanged; L1 drop behaviour is unchanged.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` (only if the source seam needs a documented hook)

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Write per-level kill-drop chance tests" (test-first). Blocks the level-gym parity and balance-evidence items.

data.description:
## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer launching a level from the curve editor, I want the gym to reproduce the game's scaled enemy counts and lengthened supply cadence, so tuning in the gym transfers to the shipped game.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Gym parity" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Add tests (in `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts` and a parity test) that:

- Launch levels 1, 5 and 10 through `GymLevel` and assert per-group enemy counts equal the game campaign's counts for the same level (shared helper, no divergent copy).
- Assert the level-gym supply cadence is lengthened by the inverse drop-chance ratio (`interval(level) = interval(1) * chance(1) / chance(level)`), so high-level gym runs are not over-supplied.
- Assert a single-wave launch (curve sequencer `_launchWave` path, `level: 0`) is treated as level 1 (no scaling, unchanged cadence).
- Assert `GymBotTuning` inherits the scaled counts and cadence (no fork).
- Assert formation gyms keep their documented scene-specific supply source and are unchanged (documented divergence).

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD (gym spawns unscaled counts and uses the flat cadence).
- Tests cover levels 1/5/10 count parity, cadence ratio, single-wave/L1 fallback, `GymBotTuning` inheritance and the unchanged formation gyms.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.test.ts`
- optionally a new `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Apply enemy-count scaling at campaign build seam" and "Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene". Blocks the level-gym parity feature.

## Goal

**User story:** As a producer, I want automated tests for the harness's per-level campaign mode, so the before/after balance evidence is trustworthy rather than hand-measured.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Automated balance evidence" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Add tests under `src/ai/eval/` that pin an **additive** per-level mode for the deterministic arena/batch:

- A run can select an explicit campaign level (at least 1, 5 and 10) and plays the real campaign waves for that level instead of the single-level spawn reservoir.
- Kill-time power-up drops use the real per-level kill-drop rule instead of seeded power-ups, while the existing seeded-drop skirmish mode stays available and unchanged.
- Same-seed runs remain byte-identical (determinism), and existing batch artifacts/report schema stay backwards compatible.
- The batch report surfaces per-level `powerUpsCollected`, `enemiesKilledByArchetype`, `avoidableHits`, `survivalSeconds` and `levelReached`.
- The mode can disable level scaling so a baseline (pre-change behaviour) can be captured with the same harness code and seeds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD (no per-level mode, seeded drops only).
- Tests cover level selection (1/5/10), real drop rule, seeded-mode compatibility, determinism and the per-level report fields.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.test.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/report.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Add level-scaling module and tunable rules", "Apply enemy-count scaling at campaign build seam", "Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene". Blocks the harness-extension feature.
